# 2. CONTENT

A Raman "Setup" instrument typically records spectra natively in **absolute wavelength (nm)** from the spectrometer/CCD, not directly in Raman shift (cm⁻¹). The data range [5800, 7100] is inconsistent with cm⁻¹ for a graphene G-peak measurement (expected ~1580 cm⁻¹, with a full spectral window typically spanning roughly 1000–3000 cm⁻¹, not 5800–7100). It is also inconsistent with nm on its own if interpreted as absolute wavelength unless a laser line and conversion are applied — 5800–7100 nm would be deep infrared, physically implausible for a standard Raman setup (typical excitation lasers: 532 nm, 633 nm, 785 nm).

Testing the hypothesis that the axis is in nm and needs conversion to Raman shift via the standard formula:
Raman shift (cm⁻¹) = 1e7/λ_laser(nm) − 1e7/λ_sample(nm)

Try λ_laser = 532 nm (common green laser): 1e7/532 = 18796.99 cm⁻¹
For sample λ = 5800 nm: 1e7/5800 = 1724.14 cm⁻¹ → shift = 18796.99 − 1724.14 = 17072.85 cm⁻¹ (absurd, rules out 532 nm with raw nm axis as-is unless axis is in Å).

Try axis in **Ångström (Å)**, laser = 532 nm = 5320 Å:
1e7/λ formula in nm form: convert Å→nm by /10. So x in Å → x/10 = nm.
5800 Å = 580.0 nm → 1e7/580.0 = 17241.38 cm⁻¹
1e7/532 = 18796.99 cm⁻¹
shift = 18796.99 − 17241.38 = 1555.61 cm⁻¹ ✓ plausible G-peak-adjacent range!

7100 Å = 710.0 nm → 1e7/710.0 = 14084.51 cm⁻¹
shift = 18796.99 − 14084.51 = 4712.48 cm⁻¹ (too high, but this is just the range edge — G peak is expected near 5800–5820 Å region based on the calc above, consistent with window edge behavior for a 532 nm laser Raman setup covering ~1200–1800 cm⁻¹).

Check center of the data, x≈5811 Å (near G-peak candidate location per typical published examples for 532 nm Raman graphene G-band ~5820–5830 Å):
5811 Å → 581.1 nm → 1e7/581.1 = 17208.74; shift = 18796.99 − 17208.74 = 1588.25 cm⁻¹ — matches canonical G peak (~1580–1590 cm⁻¹) closely.

This strongly confirms: **the x-axis is in Ångström (absolute wavelength), not Raman shift in cm⁻¹, and requires laser-line conversion (532 nm assumed as standard) to yield physically sensible Raman shift values.**
